rationale: Instrumented the append side - the gap-4 discriminator - and the draft-side run names the proposer state for the rejected history. For seed 35 the configuration change at index 4, term 2 was appended by node 2 at the same step as the first rejection (step 22) with pending_conf_index_before=2, applied_before=3, joint_before=false and validation_disabled=false. That tells two things. First, the guard's own clauses were satisfied in the ordinary way: alreadyPending was false because pendingConfIndex (2) did not exceed applied (3), and alreadyJoint was false because the appender's tracker was not joint. Second, and this is what keeps the claim unresolved rather than asserted, those operands conflict with the history the rejecting nodes hold: if node 2 had applied three entries of the same log whose index 2 is a joint-enter change, its tracker would be joint at that point, so either node 2's own entries differ from the log the others applied (a divergence the sweep's invariants did not flag because they compare committed (index, term) only at check points and only against the value first observed) or the harness produced a tracker state that its log does not imply - the restart path is a plausible source, since it rebuilds a node with the ConfState its tracker currently has while its log may already contain a joint change it has not applied. I record the operands as behaviour knowledge pending a receipt and note the next operand that would settle it: node 2's own entry types and terms for indices 1..4 at the moment of the append, which would show whether its log diverged or its tracker was rebuilt.

knowledge.statement: Draft-side observation of the append that produced the rejected history (sweep revision that records the appender's state): the joint-entering change at index 4, term 2 was appended by node 2 while pendingConfIndex was 2, applied was 3, the tracker was NOT joint and DisableConfChangeValidation was false, so both propose-time clauses were false in the ordinary way (pendingConfIndex did not exceed applied; the tracker was not joint). Every other append recorded in the same run shows the same shape - applied >= pendingConfIndex and joint_before=false - including cases where the appender had applied a dozen entries. That conflicts with the rejected nodes' history, whose index 2 is a joint-enter change: applying it in order would leave the applier joint, so the appender's tracked configuration and its log disagree at that point.
knowledge.conditions: Sweep revision with four real raft instances (node 4 registered directly and starting outside the configuration), single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, application lag skipping one node's apply about one time in six, restarts rebuilt from persisted hard state and ConfState, default DisableConfChangeValidation; operands recorded at each append (seed, step, node, entry index and term, pendingConfIndex, applied, tracker jointness, validation flag). Draft-side only: no controller receipt yet.
